messages:
harper: heads up — during the canary for the new inspect toggle I just saw an unredacted snippet land in the sampled traces. not good.
ops-bot: alert: inspect-unredact-rate spike on route /v1/embed (count=7 in 5m) :warning:
kevin: omg — any PII in those?
harper: yes, one had a raw SSN pattern in an attachment field. attaching minimal repro (sanitized except the pattern):
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/embed",
  "payload": {"attachments": ["user note: SSN: 123-45-6789"]}
}
```
sarah: thanks. quick questions: was the scrub running as expected (config-wise), or did the canary route skip the scrub step?
harper: scrub config was present, but the sampler path in the canary bypassed the fieldmask due to a header `x-inspect-bypass: 1` — looks like we mistakenly enabled that header for faster debug sampling.
lina: oof. we should avoid headers that can bypass redaction in canaries. we need a fallback for when scrub fails: instead of raw text, we pseudonymize deterministically (hash + short tag) and keep provenance metadata (non-PII).
kevin: agreed. pseudonymize is safer than raw. implementation note: deterministic HMAC with route+tenant salt so same pii -> same pseudonym across traces but not reversible. also mark sample as "pseudonymized" in metadata.
sarah: telemetry question — how do we measure incidents without storing PII? we should log counts and hashed fingerprints only. propose metrics: `inspect.unredact_attempts`, `inspect.pseudonymize_fallbacks`, and a sample of 1 in N hashed-provenance entries for debugging.
ryan: console UX: ops need a one-click lockdown that forces `inspect.mode=strip-all` for a route or tenant. also must be gated behind breakglass RBAC and audit trail. can we add that to the emergency runbook?
lina: yes — UI would flip route-level policy to `strip-all` (drop user content entirely), and backend will emit an event with `redwood.audit:inspect.lockdown` with who/when/route.
kevin: small implementation snippet for pseudonymize fallback we discussed:
```py
def pseudonymize(value, tenant_id):
    key = kdf(tenant_id)  # tenant-scoped HMAC key
    return f"[PID:{hmac_sha256(key, value)[:10]}]"
```
harper: sounds good. two questions: 1) should pseudonymize be default fallback or opt-in? 2) how quickly can we push the lockdown toggle?
sarah: fallback should be opt-in per-tenant initially (security + compliance). lockdown toggle we can ship as an ops-only console control and `redwoodctl` flag today — low-risk.
ryan: ops command ready: `redwoodctl feature set inspect.lockdown on --route /v1/embed --reason "unredact spike"` — flips to strip-all. I'll run it if we agree.
kevin: before flipping, make sure the canary samples get quarantined for forensic trace (scrubbed) and the console UI shows counts so SRE can confirm. we don't want to destroy evidence needed for root cause.
ryan: ops-bot: executing canary lockdown in 30s unless someone objects.
harper: no objections, do it. prioritize quarantine + pseudonymize fallback RFC.
ops-bot: deploy: feature inspect.lockdown set=on target=/v1/embed user=ryan (commit df3a9) :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: event logged -> redwood.audit:inspect.lockdown {route: '/v1/embed', user: 'ryan', ts: 5577654375}
lina: follow-ups: I'll open a short RFC for pseudonymize fallback (metrics, salts, KMS rotation, consent flags). Also will add the console lockdown button with RBAC and an audit modal.
sarah: and I'll add dashboard panels: `inspect_leak_rate`, `pseudonymize_fallback_rate`, plus a small sample table that only stores hashed fingerprints (no raw).
harper: thanks team. immediate mitigation done. RFC + dashboard items due EOW.
kevin: add a small unit test to ensure header `x-inspect-bypass` is ignored for canary/production routes.
ryan: noted — adding test + rollout plan.
harper: closing the thread once RFC lands. appreciate the quick moves. :thumbsup:
